title: Private Deployments: VPC & On‑Prem Deployment Guide, Day-2 Ops, Upgrade and Rollback Procedures, and Customer Requirements Library
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s recommended patterns and operational procedures for private deployments (VPC-hosted and on‑premise / air-gapped). It covers reference architectures, on‑prem packaging, day‑2 operations (monitoring, backups, scaling), upgrade and rollback procedures, and a curated customer requirements library with acceptance criteria. This is a prescriptive guide intended for Solutions Engineering, Customer Success, and SRE teams responsible for onboarding and operating private deployments.

Audience and scope
- Audience: Solutions Engineering, SRE, Customer Success, and security/compliance reviewers.
- Scope: Full lifecycle from customer requirements to installation, operationalization, upgrades, and rollback. Covers both VPC-hosted private deployments and on‑prem (air-gapped) packaging. Does not cover Redwood-hosted (public) deployments.

Owners and contacts
- Primary owner: eng-private-deployments team (owner: Aisha Patel).
- Day-to-day operations: SRE (oncall alias: #sre-private-deployments).
- Escalation: Platform lead Carlos Reyes (carlos@redwood.ai).

1) Reference architectures (high level)

A. VPC Single‑Tenant (Recommended for most enterprise customers)
- Description: Customer-managed VPC with dedicated subnets hosting Redwood control-plane components and inference nodes. Uses private subnets, NAT gateway for outbound, and optional Transit Gateway for multi-region connectivity.
- Key components:
  - Control plane services (admin API, management agents) in private subnets
  - Inference node pool (GPU instances) in private subnets with autoscaling group / ASG equivalent
  - Persistent storage (network-attached, e.g., EBS/EFS or customer-provided NFS)
  - KMS integration (customer-managed CMK) for secrets and model encryption
  - Load balancing: Internal NLB for north-south traffic between customer apps and inference endpoints
- Typical network layout: 3 AZs, public subnets for bastion/jump hosts only, private subnets per AZ for inference and control-plane.

B. VPC with Transit Gateway (Multi-VPC / Hybrid Connectivity)
- Description: For customers with existing network segmentation requirements. Redwood services placed in a dedicated VPC peered/attached to customer hub via Transit Gateway.
- Additional considerations: route table propagation, overlapping IP ranges, explicit security review for cross-VPC traffic, firewall/NVA rules.

C. On‑Prem / Air‑Gapped Reference
- Description: Packaged artifacts deployed inside customer's on‑prem datacenter or private cloud where external internet connectivity is restricted or disallowed. Uses an air-gap bundle and offline installer.
- Key constraints: no outbound telemetry by default (opt-in), offline KMS/HSM integration guidance, discrete packaging for model artifacts and runtime images.

2) Prerequisites and customer requirements (quick checklist)
- Network:
  - Non-overlapping CIDR blocks for Redwood VPCs and customer application VPCs.
  - Open required ports: 443 (control plane API), 10250 (kubelet), 2379-2380 (etcd if using managed control plane), 10255 (metrics, optional), custom ports for admin UI as agreed.
  - NAT/egress rules for service account image pulls (or offline registry).
- Security:
  - Customer KMS/HSM available for envelope encryption (recommended).
  - RBAC and SSO integration (Okta/SAML) — customer must provide IdP metadata.
- Compute & Storage:
  - GPU instance types approved (see sizing table below).
  - Network attached storage with recommended IOPS for model cache.
- Compliance:
  - Data residency requirements and allowed model artifact flows.
- Operational:
  - Designated oncall and maintenance window schedule.

3) Packaging & installation artifacts (on‑prem)

Contents of the air‑gap bundle (example)
- runtime-images.tar.gz (container images for inference runtime)
- packages/ (helm charts or kustomize manifests)
- artifacts/models/ (model binaries, checksums, licensing metadata)
- installers/install.sh (or installer.ps1 for Windows)
- offline-registry-manifest.yaml (instructions to seed private registry)
- checksums.sha256 and signed-contents.sig

Installation flow (high level)
1. Validate prerequisites (network, storage, KMS).
2. Seed private registry with runtime-images.tar.gz.
3. Apply infrastructure IaC (customer-provided Terraform modules or remote assisted Terraform run).
4. Run installer to deploy control-plane and inference runtime (e.g., helm install --namespace redwood).
5. Upload initial model artifacts and verify model serving health.

Example installer CLI snippet
- ./install.sh --namespace redwood --kubeconfig /path/to/kubeconfig --registry my-registry.local:5000 --accept-license

Example Helm values (snippet)
  replicaCount: "3"
  image:
    repository: "my-registry.local:5000/redwood/runtime"
    tag: "v2026.06.1"
  storage:
    type: "nfs"
    nfs:
      server: "10.0.10.15"
      path: "/exports/redwood"

(Ensure the above YAML is templated and validated before production rollout.)

4) Networking & security hardening

Minimum security controls
- Zero trust ingress: only allow traffic from verified customer application subnets to internal NLBs.
- Private CA or mTLS between control-plane and inference nodes.
- Key management: Use customer-managed KMS where possible; if not available, encrypt with hardware-backed keys in customer environment.
- Audit logging: Ensure audit logs are forwarded to customer SIEM.

Network ACLs / SG baseline (table described)
- Admin bastion SG: SSH (22) from customer corp CIDR only
- Control-plane SG: 443 from allowed application CIDRs, 10250 from SRE CIDRs
- Inference node SG: Internal traffic only, egress to model store endpoints and KMS

Recommendations for registries and images
- Preferred: customer-run private registry seeded with signed, versioned images.
- If registry cannot be hosted: provide alternative for direct image load onto nodes (docker load / podman load).
- Validate image signatures and checksums on every node before starting runtime.

5) Sizing, capacity, and performance guidance

Sizing guidance (example baseline)
- Small: 1-2 A10G / T4-TRT-equivalent nodes — up to 50 concurrent low-latency streams
- Medium: 4x A100-80GB or 8x A10G — typical mid-size customer (heavy batching)
- Large: Multi-node pools with sharded KV caches and model parallelism (contact Solutions Eng for throughput profiling)

Model cache and storage guidelines
- Local NVMe for hot cache (recommended: 1-2TB NVMe per GPU node).
- Shared model store (EFS/NFS) for cold artifacts with >=5000 IOPS for model pulls during scale events.

6) Day-2 operations (runbook summary)

Monitoring and observability
- Metrics: token-per-second, latency P50/P95/P99, model load times, GPU utilization, memory/KV cache hit rates.
- Dashboards: Prebuilt Grafana dashboards shipped with the package. Verify data sources: Prometheus or customer metrics endpoint.
- Logging: Sidecar logs to centralized ELK/Opensearch or customer SIEM.

Routine maintenance tasks (examples)
1. Patch OS and driver updates (monthly):
   - Validate driver compatibility with runtime (use canary nodes first).
   - Rolling reboot with cordon/drain and node-probe health checks.
2. Model rotation and refresh:
   - Upload new model artifacts to model store with versioned path and checksum.
   - Warm model cache on a small canary subset before global rollout.
3. Autoscaling policies: review schedule and usage patterns monthly.

Runbook: node reboot (quick steps)
1. Identify node (name) and confirm workload placement.
2. cordon node: kubectl cordon <node>
3. drain node with graceful timeout: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300
4. apply OS/driver patch and reboot
5. uncordon node: kubectl uncordon <node>
6. validate metrics and model-serving health for 30 minutes

7) Upgrade and rollback procedures

Principles
- All upgrades must be performed during a defined maintenance window unless high-priority security patches.
- Use canary first, then phased rollout by AZ and by subset of nodes.
- Maintain immutable rollback artifacts and clear restore points (image tags, database snapshots, model store versions).

Pre-upgrade checks (must pass)
- Backups present and verified within last 24 hours (etcd/metadata, model store index).
- Prometheus/Grafana readouts within normal baselines.
- No active critical incidents and SLOs within budget.
- Release notes reviewed and migration plan validated by Solutions Eng.

Upgrade procedure (recommended flow)
1. Announce maintenance window to stakeholders and set feature flags to reduce critical traffic.
2. Run pre-upgrade validation script: ./ops/verify_preupgrade.sh --target v2026.07.0
3. Upgrade control-plane in canary namespace: helm upgrade redwood-controlplane ./charts/controlplane -f values-canary.yaml --timeout 15m
4. Monitor health for 30 minutes: check pods, liveness/readiness, latency metrics.
5. If healthy, progressively upgrade inference node pool by AZ (use node selector and taints to limit rollout).
6. Validate model-serving with a small traffic slice (canary traffic).
7. After full rollout, run post-upgrade validation: ./ops/validate_postupgrade.sh

Rollback procedure (if upgrade fails)
1. Halt rollout and switch canary traffic back to previous control-plane (use traffic split policy in the router).
2. Rollback chart to previous revision: helm rollback redwood-controlplane <previous_revision> --timeout 10m
3. For inference nodes, drain and replace nodes with instances running previous image tag (or trigger ASG with previous launch template).
4. If metadata DB migration ran and is incompatible, restore DB snapshot and reapply pre-upgrade metadata (follow DB restore playbook).
5. Run full health validation and reopen to customer traffic only after stable for defined window (default 60 minutes).

Critical rollback notes
- Keep previous image and previous helm chart revision for at least 7 days post-upgrade.
- Document and attach logs for postmortem review.

8) Backup and restore strategy

Mandatory backups
- Metadata store (etcd / postgres) — snapshot every 6 hours, retained 14 days.
- Model store index and checksums — daily snapshot and daily integrity check.
- S3/NFS object store: lifecycle policy, and weekly integrity checks.

Restore playbook (summary)
1. Identify snapshot timestamp and confirm consistency.
2. Bring up isolated restore cluster (non-production) for verification.
3. Apply metadata snapshot, then mount model store snapshot.
4. Smoke test model loads and inference health.
5. Promote cluster to production only after passing smoke tests and stakeholder signoff.

9) Customer requirements library (selected entries)

Table (as text) of common customer requirements and acceptance criteria:
- Requirement: Data residency in EU-only region
  - Acceptance criteria: All control-plane and inference nodes deployed to eu-1 region, egress policies confirmed, audit logs stored in EU-only S3 bucket.
- Requirement: HSM-backed key management
  - Acceptance criteria: KMS/HSM integration tested with envelope encryption flow; keys never exported; attestation logs available.
- Requirement: No outbound telemetry
  - Acceptance criteria: Air-gap deployment with telemetry disabled by default; any telemetry requires signed customer opt-in.
- Requirement: FIPS 140-2 validated crypto for TLS
  - Acceptance criteria: Runtime compiled with FIPS-compatible crypto stack, documented cipher suites, and test matrix passed.
- Requirement: Offline model approval workflow
  - Acceptance criteria: Model artifacts signed and verified via customer PKI; model approval recorded in audit logs.

10) Operational checklists (quick actionable lists)

A. Pre-deployment checklist (must complete)
- Validate network architecture and CIDR plan.
- Confirm IAM roles and IdP metadata.
- Verify private registry connectivity or seed registry.
- Confirm storage IOPS and mounting permissions.
- Create incident and maintenance contacts in advance.

B. Post-deployment acceptance tests
- Control-plane API responds to health-checks in < 5s.
- Model load time for small model < 20s cold start.
- Example inference query P95 latency < SLA target (documented per customer).
- Audit logs flowing to customer SIEM.

11) Runbooks and artifacts (links)
- Deployment runbook: confluence/eng-private-deployments/private-deployments-vpc-onprem-deployment-runbook-2028-03-01.json
- Upgrade playbook: ops/playbooks/upgrade-playbook.sh (packaged in air-gap bundle)
- Backup playbook: ops/playbooks/backup-and-restore.md

12) Auditing, compliance and evidence collection

- Evidence to collect during onboarding: network diagrams, IAM roles, KMS policy, signed audit logs, vulnerability scan report.
- Retention: Audit logs retained per customer SLA (default 90 days internal, extended on request).

13) FAQs and common troubleshooting

Q: Model fails to load after scaling event
A: Check model-store latency and NFS IOPS; validate checksums; ensure model cache warming tasks ran.

Q: High P99 inference latency spikes
A: Confirm KV cache hit rate; validate batching policy and that autoscaling triggered correctly; review GPU memory pressure and fragmentation.

14) Revision history
- 2026-06-15: Initial draft (Aisha Patel)
- 2026-06-22: Added sizing guidance and on‑prem packaging checklist (reviewers: Carlos, Maya)
- 2026-07-01: Published final with upgrade & rollback procedures and customer requirements library (Aisha Patel)

Appendix: Example validation scripts and diagnostic commands
- Pre-upgrade check: ./ops/verify_preupgrade.sh --report /tmp/preupgrade-report.json
- Node health: kubectl get nodes -o wide
- Model cache status (example): curl -s http://localhost:9100/metrics | grep model_cache_hit_rate
- Backup verification: ./ops/verify_backups.sh --since 24h

If you need a tailored deployment checklist or an architecture review for a specific customer, open a PRD in the private-deployments backlog and tag the oncall SRE team for a pre-onboarding architecture review.
